# FABRIC-REPO-MIGRATION-AI: routing

This repository migrates the code and architecture of the Synapse data platform (DPV1) to Microsoft Fabric, one project at a time. Data movement is a later phase.

## Dispatch
- Migrate a source dataset (end to end) => #tool:agent:m-source-dataset
- Migrate a data product, with its DACPAC (end to end) => #tool:agent:m-data-product
- Refresh the knowledge from DPV1, check dependencies or what can start => #tool:agent:m-scope-refresher
- One step only: frame => #tool:agent:m-framer · build a stage => #tool:agent:m-builder · review => #tool:agent:m-reviewer · apply review fixes => #tool:agent:m-bug-fixer
- Validate the data of a migrated project, DPV1 => DPV2 (row counts, schema, data compare, read-only) => #tool:agent:m-data-validator
- Facts about a scope come from `5-migration-hub/knowledge/` (`python -I 0-shared/scripts/knowledge.py show|check|deps`), then only the DPV1 files it lists. Guide: [agents.md](agents.md)

## Workflows (3-workflows)
1. `wf-1-framing`: input => analysis => `4-migration-project-deliverables/<source-dataset|data-product>/<PROJECT>/1-framing/`
2. `wf-2-migration-source-dataset`: Source => databases => Files/raw (parquet, written once); APIs and files => Files/landing (as delivered) => Files/raw (parquet); then tables. One notebook per source, only where DPV1 had one. No cleansed zone (no shortcut: ingested directly from the source)
3. `wf-3-migration-data-product`: SPOT_DB source => DW/DM becomes Warehouse + DACPAC; sources exposed through `LH_INP_SDS_<SRC>` shortcuts
4. `wf-4-migration-dacpac`: dedicated-pool DACPAC => Fabric Warehouse DACPAC
5. `wf-5-data-validation`: standalone, after deployment and load: SPOT (serverless) => Lakehouse for a source; DW/DM (dedicated pool) => Warehouse silver/gold for a product; read-only, profiles from the VS Code MSSQL extension => `<project>/data-validation/`

## Rules
- DPV1 (`2-config/migration/paths.json` => `dpv1_export_root`) is read-only.
- **T-SQL stays T-SQL.** Dedicated-pool code moves through DACPAC. Only Spark notebooks and Mapping Data Flows may become notebooks.
- Every stage writes only to `4-migration-project-deliverables/<source-dataset|data-product>/<PROJECT>/<stage folder>/` and is tracked with `0-shared/scripts/track.py` (progress summary, change log, gates; see `3-workflows/wf-1-framing/stage-0-progress-tracking.md`).
- Deterministic work is done by `0-shared/scripts`; agents do analysis, translation and review.
- Naming follows `2-config/conventions` (synced from Fabric-AI-DEV-REPO; do not edit here). Convention beats legacy name; log renames.
- **Every parameter comes from `VL_MAIN`** (DEV, UAT, PRD value sets, generated by `create_variable_library.py`): pipelines read `@pipeline().libraryVariables.<NAME>`, notebooks read `notebookutils.variableLibrary.getLibrary("VL_MAIN")`. No hardcoded GUID, name, path, endpoint or secret.
- The catalog of each source is the view `[CATALOG].[<source>_catalog]`, built from its DPV1 catalog script, in the catalog warehouse (`2-config/migration/shared-platform.json`). VL_MAIN holds only where the view is: `<SRC>_CATALOG_VIEW_NAME`, `<SRC>_CATALOG_WAREHOUSE_NAME`, `<SRC>_CATALOG_WAREHOUSE_ID`, `<SRC>_CATALOG_WAREHOUSE_SQL_ENDPOINT`, `<SRC>_CATALOG_WAREHOUSE_CONN_ID`.
- **Items deploy together in one Git sync** (`3-workflows/wf-2-migration-source-dataset/deployment-design.md`): a pipeline never holds the id of another item. Lakehouse and warehouse connections use VL_MAIN expressions (`artifactId`, `endpoint`, and always `externalReferences.connection`: `<SRC>_LH_CONN_ID`, `<SRC>_CATALOG_WAREHOUSE_CONN_ID`) and `@pipeline().DataFactory` for the workspace. A missing connection fails the import with "Object reference not set"; `deploy_publish.py` refuses to publish it. No deploy tokens, no `parameter.yml`. In Fabric, pull ("Update all") before any commit from the workspace.
- **One project migration at a time.** Framing and build scripts stop when another project (either service) has a stage in progress. Finish it, or pause it (`track.py set … --status blocked --note "paused"`). `--parallel` only when the owner agreed.
- **Source Dataset Migration** identifies, maps and builds only the objects of the source dataset and their lineage. Product steps reached from a source master are marked `product` and left to Data Product Migration; data products that read the source are listed for analysis only.
- **Data Product Migration** focuses on the product: its structure, its dependencies and how it interacts with other data products. It starts only when every source dataset it is produced from is migrated (source dataset contract published, S1-S4 completed). Otherwise the scripts stop before writing anything, name the missing sources, and the agent asks the developer to migrate them first; their objects are created in `source-dataset/<SOURCE>/` only.
- **Each service stays in its lane.** A source dataset migration lists the data products that read it (analysis only) and builds nothing of them. A data product migration reads the source dataset contract (`source-dataset/<SRC>/source-dataset-contract.json`) of each input and never rebuilds a source.
- **Dependencies are in place before deployment** (standard rule, `3-workflows/wf-2-migration-source-dataset/deployment-design.md`): no artifact may depend on something a fresh Git sync cannot resolve; the reviewers check it in S5 and D6.
- **Deployability is checked at build time, not at the sync**: shortcut target ids are real GUIDs (`resolve_upstream.py`), the database project references only what it creates and reads the Lakehouse only in `[INP_<SRC>]` views, and a data product has a master and a child pipeline. `deploy_preflight.py check` and the review say it; `deploy_publish.py` refuses otherwise. The order of the steps: `3-build/deployment-runbook.md`.
- **Dedicated pool access** is read-only and documented in `2-config/migration/dedicated-pool-access.md`.
- Nothing is left behind: every DPV1 object is in a scope, the shared framework or the platform, or listed in `5-migration-hub/estate-coverage.md` with a reason. Owner decisions go to `2-config/migration/scope-decisions.json`.
- DPV1 ADLS linked services and datasets are never migrated: OneLake is built into the Lakehouse, and Fabric has no datasets.
- **Framing always asks five inputs** (service offering type, domain name, source/project name, target workspace name, deployment repo path), saved in `progress.json`. A source dataset framing also asks whether a **common catalog warehouse** (e.g. `WH_CATALOG_COMMON`) holds its catalog view: then the view goes into it and VL_MAIN reuses one `CATALOG_WAREHOUSE_*` set for every source. It also asks in which workspace that warehouse is (it may be another workspace than the target one: the item is then built in that workspace's folder and the pipelines read `CATALOG_WAREHOUSE_WORKSPACE_ID`); `resolve_catalog.py` reads the workspace, warehouse and SQL endpoint IDs from Fabric. The artifacts are kept in the project folder and stored in `<deployment repo>/<workspace folder>/` with `deploy_publish.py` after each passing stage review.
- **Names in this repository are lowercase** (folders and files, e.g. `m-framer.agent.md`, `source-dataset/geos/`), like Fabric-AI-DEV-REPO. Exceptions: `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `SKILL.md` (tools look for these names) and files synced from the baseline. **Generated Fabric artifacts keep the Fabric naming convention** (`LH_SDS_GEOS`, `DP_SDS_CONST`, `PL_*`, `NB_*`): they are copied unchanged to the deployment repo.
- **Short pages.** Each output page shows what its reader needs; reference detail goes to the `analysis/` folder of its stage (`1-framing/analysis/`, `3-build/analysis/`). A page that grows hard to read is split. Generated, rebuildable data stays out of Git: `2-legacy-code/` (extract_scope_code.py), `5-migration-hub/knowledge/`, `migration-map.json`, `refresh-report.md` (refresh_hub.py).
- Pause between stages. Ask with multiple-choice questions plus an "other" option. Spell out acronyms on first use. Write in English.

**After changing a script in `0-shared/scripts`:** run `python -I 0-shared/scripts/selftest.py`. It rebuilds RMA in a scratch copy and must give the committed build, with the review and preflight clean. Generated working files live in `3-build/_work/` (ignore them); the files to read are `fabric-deployment/`, `build-notes/` and `deployment-runbook.md`.
